Findings are limited to local Procedure element, constraint, type, target, binding, and semantic changes. Snapshot differences inherited only from `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, `Extension`, `BackboneElement`, or other base artifacts are excluded from `findings[]` per the assignment rule.

Changes to base datatypes such as CodeableReference, Reference, CodeableConcept, BackboneElement, and Element except where Procedure locally changes an element type to or from those datatypes.
SearchParameter, OperationDefinition, CapabilityStatement, compartment, profile, implementation guide, and server behavior changes for Procedure.

oldArtifact.identityNotesMd: R4 package index confirms `StructureDefinition-Procedure.json` with id/type `Procedure`.

newArtifact.name: Procedure
newArtifact.identityNotesMd: The R6 counterpart is present at the assigned path with the same canonical URL, id, type, kind, derivation, and baseDefinition. No rename/split/merge at artifact identity level was detected; status changed from draft to active and is not itself treated as breaking.

narrativeReportMd:
# Procedure R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found. `Procedure` keeps the same canonical identity, but R6 makes multiple local wire-format changes: timing is renamed from `performed[x]` to `occurrence[x]`; several code/reference pairs are collapsed into `CodeableReference`; `outcome` changes both cardinality and datatype; and several R4 elements are removed.

## Scope
I compared the local R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions, package indexes, package metadata, the assignment manifest, selected terminology files for `Procedure.status`, and the R6 `CodeableReference` datatype. Inherited Resource/DomainResource/Base datatype changes are listed out of scope and not counted as Procedure findings.

## Main migration themes
The largest theme is `CodeableReference` adoption: reasons, used items, complications, follow-up, and outcomes all need explicit shape conversion. The second theme is Procedure becoming less patient-only: R6 permits non-patient subjects and adds modifier `focus`. The third theme is R6-to-R4 loss: new targets and elements such as `bodyStructure`, `recorded`, `reported[x]`, and `supportingInfo` have no R4 base representation.

## Highest-impact findings
High-impact findings are the `performed[x]`→`occurrence[x]` rename, the `reason`/`used` merges, the complication and outcome datatype changes, the removal of protocol-instantiation and asserter fields, and the broadened subject/focus semantics.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for removed fields without exact replacements (`instantiatesCanonical`, `instantiatesUri`, `asserter`), the new performer `prc-1` invariant, subject/focus workflow implications, and mapping existing R4 body-structure extensions to the new R6 `bodyStructure`.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many hard breaks could have been softened by retaining deprecated aliases or adding separate reference elements. The R6 design is often semantically cleaner, especially where `CodeableReference` keeps code/reference pairs together, but it requires real migration transforms.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze base artifacts for inherited changes, `CodeableReference` for datatype-level compatibility, and Procedure SearchParameters/compartments for runtime effects of non-patient subjects.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Procedure` has high-impact local breaking changes despite stable artifact identity. Top concerns are renamed/removed elements, broad CodeableReference datatype replacements, and non-patient Procedure semantics. Main uncertainty is the intended official mapping for removed provenance/protocol fields.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be transform-driven, not validator-only. Map renamed choices (`performed*` to `occurrence*`), wrap R4 CodeableConcepts into CodeableReference `.concept`, wrap R4 references into `.reference`, and define policies for R6 content that R4 cannot carry. Runtime code must also stop assuming Procedure is always patient-centered.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural and validation-impact findings because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared, with package indexes confirming identity. Confidence is medium for some justification and terminology/picklist implications because official diffs, ballot rationale, real terminology expansions, and cross-version ConceptMaps were not available.

findings.title: Procedure.performed[x] was renamed to Procedure.occurrence[x], with Timing added as a new choice type

oldState.summary: R4 represented procedure timing as performed[x] with dateTime, Period, string, Age, or Range.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 JSON uses choice properties such as `performedDateTime`, `performedPeriod`, `performedString`, `performedAge`, and `performedRange`.

newState.summary: R6 represents the same timing concept as occurrence[x] and also permits Timing.

semanticText.short: When the procedure occurred or is occurring

newState.narrativeMd: R6 JSON uses choice properties such as `occurrenceDateTime`, `occurrencePeriod`, and the new `occurrenceTiming`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element names differ, but the cardinality, summary flag, and all R4 choice types are preserved, and the definitions are near-identical timing descriptions. R6 adds clarifying text and the `Timing` choice.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct wire-format and generated-model break. An R4 instance containing `performedDateTime` or any other `performed[x]` choice will contain an unknown element under the R6 StructureDefinition; the value must be moved to the matching `occurrence[x]` property. R6 `occurrenceTiming` has no R4 `performedTiming` counterpart, so it needs a lossy transform, extension, or profile-specific mapping when converting to R4. Generated classes, serializers, FHIRPath expressions, search extraction, and migration scripts that use the R4 property name or R4 datatype shape need explicit conversion rather than a version label change.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Procedure timing is clinically important for sequencing and audit. Dropping it during migration can change encounter chronology and downstream analytics.

justification.inferredGoal: Align event timing terminology around occurrence[x] and allow recurring/ongoing Timing.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `performed[x]` in the base resource, update its definition, and add `Timing` as an additional choice type.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goals of clearer occurrence timing and support for ongoing or recurring `Timing` are reasonable. The hard rename from `performed[x]` to `occurrence[x]` is not clearly necessary for those goals, because the functional enhancement could have been added to the existing choice element with clearer wording.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could retain `Procedure.performed[x]` at the same path, add `Timing` to its allowed types, and revise the definition/comment to explain occurrence versus requested timing. That would preserve R4-valid instances; the tradeoff is living with the older name and relying on documentation or search aliases for event-pattern consistency.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 data and generated code but leaves Procedure with a less event-consistent element name.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Procedure.performed[x]` as 0..1 with dateTime, Period, string, Age, and Range.
R6 defines `Procedure.occurrence[x]` as 0..1 with the R4 choice types plus Timing.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments illustrate the changed choice-property names; complete valid instances may require other optional context.

findings.narrativeMd: `Procedure.performed[x]` is no longer present in R6 and is replaced by `Procedure.occurrence[x]`. This is the most common kind of hard instance break for FHIR JSON/XML because choice element names are part of the serialized property name. Existing R4 data with any `performed*` property must be transformed, not merely revalidated as R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: yes, whenever an R4 instance carries a `performed[x]` value. R6 validators expect the `occurrence[x]` choice name. R6-valid/not-R4-representable also occurs for `occurrenceTiming`, because R4 had no Timing choice for this element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map each R4 `performedDateTime`, `performedPeriod`, `performedString`, `performedAge`, and `performedRange` to the corresponding R6 `occurrence*` property. Decide a policy for R6 `occurrenceTiming` when producing R4: extension, narrative/text, derived Period, or rejection. Regression tests should cover every choice type.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The rename likely improves consistency with event patterns, but a deprecated R4 alias would have been backward compatible. Without an alias, all wire-format parsers and generated models must update.

findings.title: Procedure.reasonCode and Procedure.reasonReference were replaced by Procedure.reason CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 had separate repeating elements for coded reasons and referenced reason resources.
oldState.narrativeMd: `reasonCode` carried CodeableConcept values; `reasonReference` carried references. R4 comments advised not duplicating the same reason across both.

newState.summary: R6 has one repeating CodeableReference element that can carry a concept, a reference, or both.

semanticText.comment: If both Procedure.reason.concept and Procedure.reason.reference are present, they are expected to be consistent with each other.

newState.narrativeMd: The target reference set is materially the same, but the serialized shape and model property are different.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The definitions, cardinality, binding name, and reference targets show that R6 intentionally merges the two R4 reason elements into one CodeableReference-valued element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance using `reasonCode` or `reasonReference` has R4-only property names and will not validate against R6 until converted to `reason[].concept` or `reason[].reference`. R6 can also place concept and reference in the same CodeableReference item; R4 can represent both facts only as separate arrays, losing the explicit pairing/consistency relationship.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Reasons for a procedure drive clinical interpretation, quality measurement, and authorization logic. Losing the relationship between a reason code and a referenced resource can affect decision support.

justification.inferredGoal: Use CodeableReference to avoid parallel code/reference elements and allow a reason concept and exact reason resource to stay associated.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` while adding `reason` CodeableReference.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using CodeableReference for Procedure reasons is a coherent R6 goal because it lets one item carry a code, a reference, or a consistent pair. A compatibility design exists, but it would keep parallel old fields beside the new field and require conflict and pairing rules, so the breaking simplification is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` as deprecated aliases while introducing `reason`. That would preserve R4 wire format for legacy data, but it only partially meets the R6 goal: old arrays do not preserve item-level associations, and allowing both old and new fields risks inconsistent duplicate reasons indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances but duplicates reason representation and the old split fields cannot express paired concept/reference semantics cleanly.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `reasonCode` as repeating CodeableConcept with an example procedure-reason binding.
R4 defines `reasonReference` as repeating Reference to Condition, Observation, Procedure, DiagnosticReport, or DocumentReference.
R6 defines `reason` as repeating CodeableReference with the same reference targets and procedure-reason example binding.

examples.examplesMd: R4 can carry concept and reference in separate elements; R6 can pair them within one CodeableReference.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 removes the two R4 reason elements and introduces a single `Procedure.reason` CodeableReference. This is locally breaking for instances and code because both old property names disappear and CodeableReference nests the concept/reference under different child names.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: yes for R4 instances that populate either removed element. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: partial, because a CodeableReference with both concept and reference can only be split into R4 `reasonCode` and `reasonReference`, losing item-level association.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map each R4 `reasonCode[]` item to `reason[].concept` and each `reasonReference[]` item to `reason[].reference`. Where source systems know a code and reference describe the same reason, pair them in one R6 CodeableReference. For R6→R4, split concept/reference and document that pairing is lost unless preserved in an extension.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is understandable as part of the wider CodeableReference adoption, but the removal of old fields was avoidable through deprecated aliases or a transition invariant.

findings.title: Procedure.usedCode and Procedure.usedReference were replaced by Procedure.used CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 had separate repeating coded and referenced items used during the procedure.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented coded used items in `usedCode` and referenced Device/Medication/Substance instances in `usedReference`.

newState.summary: R6 has one repeating CodeableReference element and adds BiologicallyDerivedProduct as a reference target.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 also changes the example binding canonical from device-kind to device-type and updates the comment to refer to `Procedure.focalDevice.manipulated`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `used` definition and requirements match R4 `usedReference`, while CodeableReference subsumes R4 `usedCode`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with `usedCode` or `usedReference` use properties that do not exist in R6. R6 instances can refer to BiologicallyDerivedProduct and can pair a concept with a reference in one CodeableReference, neither of which maps cleanly to R4 without loss or extension.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Used items can be important for device/medication traceability, contamination investigations, and supply-chain analytics.

justification.inferredGoal: Adopt CodeableReference and support biologically derived products as procedure inputs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `usedCode` and `usedReference`, possibly widening the old reference targets, while adding `used` CodeableReference.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adopting CodeableReference and adding BiologicallyDerivedProduct support are reasonable R6 goals. The less-breaking path would reduce migration failures but would also perpetuate the parallel code/reference pattern that the R6 model is trying to remove.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative could keep `usedCode` and `usedReference` as deprecated, add BiologicallyDerivedProduct to the legacy reference target set, and add `used` for new CodeableReference content. This preserves many R4 instances, but systems would need reconciliation rules if both forms are populated and the old fields still cannot express a single coded-and-referenced used item.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Covers legacy code/reference cases but leaves duplicate item-used representations and only the new field cleanly supports concept/reference pairing.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `usedCode` as CodeableConcept with example binding to device-kind.
R4 defines `usedReference` as Reference(Device, Medication, Substance).
R6 defines `used` as CodeableReference(Device, Medication, Substance, BiologicallyDerivedProduct) with example binding to device-type.

examples.examplesMd: The BiologicallyDerivedProduct example highlights a new R6 target outside the R4 allowed target set.

findings.narrativeMd: `Procedure.usedCode` and `Procedure.usedReference` are no longer present. R6 uses a single `Procedure.used` CodeableReference, changes the example terminology binding, and expands the reference target domain.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: yes for any R4 instance using either old `used*` element. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: possible for BiologicallyDerivedProduct targets or combined concept/reference items.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `usedCode[]` to `used[].concept` and `usedReference[]` to `used[].reference`. Review traceability use cases to decide how to handle R6 BiologicallyDerivedProduct in R4, typically via an extension or explicit rejection.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The CodeableReference design provides a cleaner model, but backward-compatible aliases would have reduced instance and code-generation disruption.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The binding strength is example, so the value-set change is not a validation break by itself; terminology expansion would improve confidence about migration implications for coded `used` concepts.

findings.title: Procedure.complication changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference and absorbs complicationDetail

oldState.summary: R4 complication was a repeating CodeableConcept; complicationDetail was a separate repeating Reference(Condition).
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 separated textual/coded complications from Condition resources documenting the complication.

newState.summary: R6 complication is a repeating CodeableReference to Condition and is now included in summary.
newState.narrativeMd: The old `complicationDetail` property is removed, and coded complications must move under `complication[].concept`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: R6 `complication` preserves the condition-code example binding and adds the Condition target formerly held by `complicationDetail`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 `complication` array items are CodeableConcept objects and therefore have the wrong R6 shape unless wrapped as `concept`. Existing `complicationDetail` references use a removed property. R6 summary responses may now include complications where R4 summary handling did not.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Complications are clinically significant adverse outcomes. Silent loss or failure to display them during migration can affect safety review and quality reporting.

justification.inferredGoal: Unify coded and referenced complications and allow a code/reference pair for the same complication.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `complication` CodeableConcept and `complicationDetail` Reference as deprecated while adding CodeableReference support.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A unified CodeableReference complication is a reasonable model for coded and Condition-backed complications. Retaining both R4 fields would protect old instances, but it would create competing same-resource representations for a safety-relevant fact and undermine the cleaner R6 shape.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained the R4 `complication` and `complicationDetail` paths and introduced a new CodeableReference path or alias. That alternative is incomplete because the old paths do not preserve a code/reference pair as one complication, and it would require long-term conflict handling between deprecated and new complication carriers.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy complication data but splits clinically important complication representation, summary behavior, and search semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `complication` as repeating CodeableConcept and not summary.
R4 defines `complicationDetail` as repeating Reference(Condition).
R6 defines `complication` as repeating CodeableReference(Condition) and summary=true.

examples.examplesMd: R6 can pair the coded complication and Condition reference in a way R4 could only approximate through separate arrays.

findings.narrativeMd: The complication representation changes from separate code and detail fields into a single CodeableReference field. This is both a serialized datatype change and an element removal. It is also notable for `_summary` behavior because `complication` becomes summary in R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: yes when R4 carries direct CodeableConcept complications or `complicationDetail`. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: partial when a single R6 item pairs concept and reference. Summary payloads can also differ between versions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap R4 `complication[]` values as `complication[].concept` and map `complicationDetail[]` references as `complication[].reference`. If both exist and are known to describe the same event, pair them; otherwise keep separate R6 items. Test summary-mode extraction and adverse-event reporting workflows.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The merged design is clinically useful but a compatibility alias for `complicationDetail` would have avoided a hard break for existing references.

findings.title: Procedure.outcome changed from a single CodeableConcept to repeating CodeableReference(Observation)

oldState.summary: R4 outcome was optional, single, and CodeableConcept.

semanticText.definition: The outcome of the procedure - did it resolve the reasons for the procedure being performed?

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4 JSON, `outcome` is a single object with CodeableConcept fields such as `coding` or `text`.

newState.summary: R6 outcome is optional, repeating, and CodeableReference to Observation.

semanticText.definition: The short term outcome of the procedure assessed during the procedure, at the conclusion of the procedure, during the immediate post-performance period, or at discharge.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6 JSON, `outcome` is an array of CodeableReference objects; coded outcomes are nested under `concept` and Observation references under `reference`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This changes both JSON cardinality shape and datatype. A valid R4 object-valued `outcome` is not an R6 array of CodeableReference. Conversely, R6 can carry multiple outcomes and Observation references that cannot be represented in the single R4 CodeableConcept without loss.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Outcomes affect clinical quality and procedure success assessment. Losing Observation-backed outcomes can reduce clinical specificity.

justification.inferredGoal: Support multiple short-term outcomes and precise Observation-backed outcomes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep singleton CodeableConcept `outcome` and add separate repeating Observation-backed outcome details.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 comments give concrete reasons for multiple short-term, Observation-backed outcomes, so the expressiveness goal is strong. A less-breaking additive design is possible, but it would not provide one uniform repeating outcome list and would create persistent mapping ambiguity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial alternative could leave `Procedure.outcome` as `0..1 CodeableConcept` and add an optional repeating element for additional or Observation-backed outcomes. This would preserve R4 instances, but implementers would need rules for which outcome is primary, how searches combine the two locations, and how to avoid divergent coded and referenced outcome statements.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old coded outcomes but creates primary/additional outcome distinctions and duplicate search/mapping rules.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `outcome` as 0..1 CodeableConcept.
R6 defines `outcome` as 0..* CodeableReference with targetProfile Observation.
R6 comments describe multiple short-term outcomes and Observation-backed outcomes.
evidence.quote: Procedure.outcome are short term outcomes because long term outcomes are typically documented as Observations.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example is intentionally object-valued; the R6 equivalent must be an array and must wrap coded content under `concept`.

findings.narrativeMd: `Procedure.outcome` keeps its path but not its representation. It becomes repeating and changes to CodeableReference(Observation), while the definition narrows toward short-term outcomes. This is a high-impact change because the property name alone is not enough to make an R4 payload valid R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: yes when `outcome` is present in R4. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: high for multiple outcomes and Observation references. Code generators also change from an optional CodeableConcept property to a list of CodeableReference values.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Convert an R4 `outcome` object to a one-item R6 array with `concept`. For R6→R4, only a single concept-only outcome maps cleanly; multiple outcomes or Observation references require extensions, a linked Observation strategy, or manual selection rules.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The use case for multiple Observation-backed outcomes seems strong, but a separate additive element could have avoided changing the existing property shape. The tradeoff would be more fields and more mapping rules.

findings.title: Procedure.followUp changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference(ServiceRequest | PlanDefinition)

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 follow-up instructions were coded/textual values directly in the array.

newState.summary: R6 followUp is repeating CodeableReference to ServiceRequest or PlanDefinition.

semanticText.definition: R6 adds that CarePlan can reference the Procedure via CarePlan.addresses.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can refer directly to follow-up requests or definitions, while coded text must be nested as `concept`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The array remains repeating, but the item datatype changes. Direct R4 CodeableConcept items are invalid as R6 CodeableReference items unless wrapped in `concept`. R6 references to ServiceRequest or PlanDefinition have no direct R4 followUp representation.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Follow-up instructions can affect care continuity, so dropped references or text are clinically relevant.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow follow-up to point to actionable requests or reusable definitions while preserving coded/text instructions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `followUp` CodeableConcept and add a separate follow-up request or definition reference element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing follow-up to point to actionable ServiceRequest or PlanDefinition resources is a reasonable R6 goal. The compatible design would preserve old payloads, but it would keep the same parallel pattern that CodeableReference is intended to consolidate.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept `followUp` as CodeableConcept and added a new optional reference element for ServiceRequest or PlanDefinition. That would avoid invalidating R4 `followUp` arrays, but it only partially meets the goal because follow-up instructions would be split across two fields and systems would need reconciliation rules when both are present.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy instructions but perpetuates parallel code/reference follow-up representation and conflict rules.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `followUp` as repeating CodeableConcept.
R6 defines `followUp` as repeating CodeableReference(ServiceRequest, PlanDefinition).

examples.examplesMd: R6 reference-valued follow-up needs an R4 extension or out-of-band linked request.

findings.narrativeMd: `Procedure.followUp` changes item type from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference. This is less disruptive than a rename but still hard-breaking for serialized instances because the item shape changes.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: yes for populated R4 followUp arrays. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: yes for ServiceRequest or PlanDefinition references unless represented through extensions or separate resources not connected by the R4 element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap R4 follow-up codes/text as `followUp[].concept`. For R6 references, decide whether to preserve a reference extension, generate a textual CodeableConcept summary, or maintain the linked request externally.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A separate additive reference element would have been less breaking but would perpetuate parallel elements.

findings.title: Procedure.instantiatesCanonical and Procedure.instantiatesUri were removed

oldState.summary: R4 allowed Procedure to declare canonical or external protocols, guidelines, order sets, or definitions it instantiates.
oldState.narrativeMd: The two R4 elements were both summary elements and supported FHIR canonical references and arbitrary external URI identifiers.

newState.summary: No local Procedure element in R6 carries the same canonical/URI instantiation role.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 Procedure differential and snapshot do not contain `instantiatesCanonical` or `instantiatesUri`.

facts.note: No same-name or obvious local replacement was present in the R6 Procedure StructureDefinition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance using either instantiates element contains a property that is absent from R6 Procedure. The data is summary-level protocol/guideline provenance, so strict validators and generated models will reject or drop it unless explicitly mapped to an extension or another workflow artifact.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Protocol or guideline adherence can matter for quality, research, and authorization workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Possibly move protocol/guideline linkage out of Procedure or rely on basedOn/PlanDefinition workflows.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `instantiatesCanonical` and `instantiatesUri` as deprecated base elements until an explicit replacement exists.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The computable R6 Procedure definition removes both instantiation links without showing an equivalent base replacement. If the goal was to move protocol or guideline linkage elsewhere, retaining the old fields with deprecation guidance would have preserved existing data while still steering new implementations away from them.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `instantiatesCanonical` and `instantiatesUri` at `0..*`, mark them deprecated, and document any preferred R6 linkage pattern. That preserves all R4-valid instances using these fields; the tradeoff is some legacy surface area in Procedure until a clearer replacement is standardized.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Leaves optional legacy protocol-link fields in Procedure, but their semantics are clear and the compatibility cost is modest.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `instantiatesCanonical` as repeating canonical targeting PlanDefinition, ActivityDefinition, Measure, OperationDefinition, and Questionnaire.
R4 defines `instantiatesUri` as repeating uri.
No R6 Procedure element with id `Procedure.instantiatesCanonical` or `Procedure.instantiatesUri` was present.

examples.examplesMd: The migration extension URL is illustrative only; an official cross-version extension or local IG extension should be chosen.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 Procedure could directly identify protocols or definitions it instantiated. R6 removes both direct elements, so this information has no computable home in the base R6 Procedure definition found in the package.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: yes if either element is populated. R6-to-R4 is not the main risk because the R6 element is absent; the main issue is preserving R4 protocol-link information during upgrade.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory Procedure instances with either instantiates element. If the information is needed, map it to an approved extension, a related request/PlanDefinition workflow, or Provenance/metadata according to local policy. Test that summary exports do not silently drop it.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This removal appears avoidable from the supplied evidence. A deprecated retained element or explicit replacement would have preserved data while allowing guidance to move elsewhere.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review should confirm whether the R6 ballot narrative or change proposals identify a preferred replacement.

findings.title: Procedure.asserter was removed; R6 adds reported[x] and recorded but no exact replacement

oldState.summary: R4 had an optional summary Reference identifying the person asserting the procedure statement.

semanticText.definition: Individual who is making the procedure statement.

oldState.narrativeMd: `asserter` was distinct from `recorder`: it identified who made the assertion, not necessarily who entered the record.

newState.summary: R6 has no `asserter`; it adds `recorded` and `reported[x]`, and retains `recorder` with explanatory comments.
newState.narrativeMd: `reported[x]` can indicate secondary reported status or source, but it is not a one-for-one replacement for the assertion author semantics of R4 `asserter`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The added R6 reported/recorded elements occupy related provenance territory, but neither definition exactly states “individual making the procedure statement.”

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with `asserter` will fail strict R6 validation because the property is gone. If blindly mapped to `reportedReference`, semantics may change from assertion author to source of a reported record.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Attribution affects trust, audit, and medico-legal interpretation of historical procedure statements.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify provenance through recorder, recorded, reported[x], and Provenance rather than a Procedure-specific asserter.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `asserter` as deprecated while adding `recorded`, `reported[x]`, and provenance guidance.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying Procedure provenance through recorder, reported source, and Provenance is reasonable, but the R6 elements are not exact replacements for every R4 asserter. Removing `asserter` forces lossy or policy-dependent migration where a deprecated retained field would have preserved attribution.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `Procedure.asserter` as deprecated and explain when new content should use `recorder`, `reported[x]`, or Provenance instead. This keeps one legacy provenance element, but the cost is moderate compared with invalidating R4 instances and requiring implementers to guess the intended semantic mapping.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Maintains an overlapping provenance shortcut, but avoids unsafe remapping and preserves attribution semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `asserter` as 0..1 Reference(Patient, RelatedPerson, Practitioner, PractitionerRole).
No R6 Procedure element with id `Procedure.asserter` was present.
R6 adds `reported[x]` for secondary reported records and possible source of report.

migrationExampleJson.note: Only use this mapping if the R4 asserter is truly the report source; otherwise preserve in Provenance or extension.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is conditional because the semantics are not identical.

findings.narrativeMd: The R4 `asserter` element disappears. R6 adds provenance-like fields, but the definitions do not establish a safe automatic mapping for all cases.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: yes when `asserter` is present. R6-to-R4 risk is lower for this specific field because R6 lacks the old field, but R6 `reported[x]` may also be hard to back-port without a local R4 extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not blindly map every `asserter` to `reportedReference`. Classify whether the asserter is the report source, recorder, performer, or provenance agent. Use `reportedReference`, `recorder`, Provenance, or an extension according to that classification.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal was avoidable through deprecation. Human review is needed to confirm the intended replacement pattern in ballot narrative or cross-version guidance.

findings.title: New prc-1 invariant forbids onBehalfOf when performer.actor resolves to Practitioner or PractitionerRole

oldState.summary: R4 allowed performer.onBehalfOf with Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Device, Organization, Patient, or RelatedPerson actors; no local invariant restricted Practitioner/PractitionerRole actors.

semanticText.definition: The organization the device or practitioner was acting on behalf of.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 requirements explicitly mentioned practitioners and devices being associated with multiple organizations.

newState.summary: R6 adds error invariant prc-1 and changes actor semantics to include people, organizations, devices, CareTeam, and HealthcareService.

constraints.human: Procedure.performer.onBehalfOf can only be populated when performer.actor isn't Practitioner or PractitionerRole
constraints.expression: onBehalfOf.exists() and actor.resolve().exists() implies actor.resolve().where($this is Practitioner or $this is PractitionerRole).empty()

semanticText.definition: The Organization the Patient, RelatedPerson, Device, CareTeam, and HealthcareService was acting on behalf of.

newState.narrativeMd: The invariant is resolution-dependent: it fires when the actor reference can be resolved and the resolved resource is Practitioner or PractitionerRole.

facts.newValue: onBehalfOf.exists() and actor.resolve().exists() implies actor.resolve().where($this is Practitioner or $this is PractitionerRole).empty()

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 performer with a Practitioner or PractitionerRole actor and `onBehalfOf` Organization was structurally allowed. In R6, a validator with reference resolution can reject that combination as an error. Impact depends on whether validation resolves references and on local use of `onBehalfOf` for practitioners.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrectly dropping acting-on-behalf-of organization can affect attribution, billing, audit, and accountability.

justification.inferredGoal: Restrict onBehalfOf to actor types where the organization cannot already be represented by practitioner role or equivalent affiliation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make `prc-1` warning-level or prohibit only the clearest duplicate-affiliation cases.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of avoiding `onBehalfOf` where actor affiliation is already represented is reasonable. The supplied definitions do not show why an error-level invariant had to reject R4 practitioner or PractitionerRole patterns immediately, especially when migration may require PractitionerRole, Provenance, or local affiliation data.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial less-breaking design could express `prc-1` as a best-practice warning, stage it through a profile, or narrowly prohibit only cases where the actor already carries the same organization. That would preserve more R4 instances, but it would not give base R6 consumers the same guarantee that `onBehalfOf` is absent for practitioner-affiliation cases.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves existing attribution but weakens uniform base enforcement and may leave redundant practitioner affiliation data.

evidence.detail: R4 definition says the organization the device or practitioner was acting on behalf of.
R6 adds an error invariant restricting onBehalfOf when actor resolves to Practitioner or PractitionerRole.
evidence.quote: onBehalfOf.exists() and actor.resolve().exists() implies actor.resolve().where($this is Practitioner or $this is PractitionerRole).empty()

evidence.detail: R6 adds CareTeam and HealthcareService as performer.actor targets.

migrationExampleJson.note: One possible migration is to represent the practitioner organization through PractitionerRole and omit onBehalfOf if that matches local semantics.

examples.examplesMd: The old-valid/new-invalid example assumes the validator can resolve `Practitioner/pr1`; without resolution, the FHIRPath expression may not fire.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a local invariant on the performer backbone. The new rule changes validation behavior for a common attribution pattern: a practitioner acting on behalf of an organization.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: potential, because the invariant depends on reference resolution. R6-to-R4 risk also exists because R6 performer actors can now be CareTeam or HealthcareService, which R4 did not allow.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Search for performer entries with both `actor` and `onBehalfOf`. For Practitioner/PractitionerRole actors, decide whether the organization should be represented through PractitionerRole, Provenance, affiliation data, or an extension. Include validator tests with resolvable references so the invariant is actually exercised.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A warning or best-practice invariant would have been less breaking. The stricter R6 rule may be justified if PractitionerRole is the intended representation for practitioner affiliation, but that rationale is not explicit in the supplied StructureDefinition.

findings.title: Procedure subject scope broadened beyond Patient/Group and a new modifier focus element was added

oldState.summary: R4 Procedure was defined as an action on or for a patient, with subject Reference(Patient | Group).

semanticText.definition: The person, animal or group on which the procedure was performed.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 implementations often safely assumed Procedure.subject was patient-like.

newState.summary: R6 allows subject Reference(Patient | Group | Device | Practitioner | Organization | Location) and adds modifier `focus` for target distinct from subject of record.

semanticText.definition: On whom or on what the procedure was performed... If the actual focus of the procedure is different from the subject, the focus element specifies the actual focus of the procedure.

newState.narrativeMd: The root Procedure definition now includes procedures on practitioners, devices, organizations, or locations such as inspections or accreditation.

facts.oldValue: performed on or for a patient
facts.newValue: performed on or for a patient, practitioner, device, organization, or location

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break because R4 Patient/Group subjects remain allowed. It is a major runtime and down-conversion risk: R4 code, database schemas, search logic, and patient-compartment assumptions may expect Procedure.subject to resolve only to Patient or Group. R6 `focus` is modifier=true, so consumers must not ignore it when present because it can change the target of the procedure.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misclassifying a procedure on a device, location, organization, practitioner, or caregiver as a patient procedure can affect safety inspections, credentialing, and patient-record interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow Procedure to represent non-patient procedures such as inspections, licensing/accreditation, and education/counseling focus scenarios.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because R4 Patient and Group subjects remain valid and `focus` is optional.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 definitions explicitly document non-patient Procedure use cases and the modifier `focus` semantics. This is a broad model change with real implementation impact, but it widens the base model rather than invalidating R4 Patient/Group Procedure instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because the change is target widening plus an optional new modifier element, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable for R4-to-R6 preservation. Profiles or separate resources would reduce the breadth of core Procedure, but they would mainly constrain new R6 use cases rather than avoid an R4-to-R6 base validation break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is R6-to-R4 loss and patient-centric runtime assumptions in R6 consumers, not preservation of R4 instances.

evidence.detail: R4 root short/definition describe an action performed on a patient.
R4 subject targets only Patient and Group.
R6 subject adds Device, Practitioner, Organization, and Location.
R6 adds `focus` as modifier=true and summary=true.

examples.examplesMd: The extension URL is illustrative. R4 has no base element for non-Patient/Group subject targets or Procedure.focus.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 materially changes what a Procedure can be about. It is no longer only patient/group-centered; it can describe procedures on entities such as devices, locations, organizations, and practitioners. The new `focus` element is a modifier because it can alter the actual target when the subject is just the record context.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: no for ordinary R4 subjects. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: high for non-Patient/Group subjects and any use of `focus`. Runtime risk is high for code that casts subject to Patient, assigns procedures to patient compartments without checking target type, or ignores modifier elements.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit code paths that assume `Procedure.subject.reference` starts with `Patient/` or `Group/`. Add type-aware handling and explicit tests for Device, Practitioner, Organization, and Location subjects. For R6→R4, either reject non-patient procedures, map through profiles/extensions, or preserve them outside R4 Procedure.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The broader model appears intentional and useful. A less disruptive path would have been profiles or separate resources, but that would reduce core consistency for event-like actions on non-patient entities.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Compartment membership and search-parameter behavior were not analyzed here and should be checked separately if Procedure subject broadening affects server behavior.

findings.title: Procedure.category cardinality widened from 0..1 to 0..*

oldState.summary: R4 allowed at most one category.
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4 JSON, `category` is a single CodeableConcept object when present.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6 JSON, `category` is an array because the maximum is repeating.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4-to-R6 is structurally safe for absent or single category values, though parsers and generated models change the property from singleton to array in R6. R6 instances with multiple categories cannot be represented in the base R4 element without choosing one, combining codings, or using an extension.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow multiple classifications for search, sorting, and display.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `category` as a singleton and add an optional repeating secondary or additional category element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting multiple classifications for search, sorting, and display is reasonable. Changing the existing singleton element to repeating creates avoidable wire and generated-model churn for populated R4 category data, while an additive secondary-category path could meet most of the same goal.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could leave `Procedure.category` at `0..1` and add a new `additionalCategory` or similarly named repeating element for extra classifications. This would preserve R4-valid instances and still allow multiple classifications; the tradeoff is a less elegant split model and the need for validators, search, and display code to union the primary and additional categories.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 wire shape but adds primary/additional category semantics and requires search rules to cover both fields.

evidence.detail: R4 max cardinality is 1.
R6 max cardinality is *.

examples.examplesMd: Multiple R6 category values require a local down-conversion policy for R4.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a widening, not an R4-to-R6 validation break. It is still material for code generation and round-tripping because singleton-versus-array cardinality changes the JSON shape and typed model.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: no. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: yes for multiple categories. Runtime code that expects a singleton category must be updated for R6.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated models and mapping code to treat R6 category as repeating. For R6→R4, define a deterministic primary-category selection or an extension for extra categories.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The widening is relatively safe upward but unavoidable if the base model needs multiple categories. A secondary-category extension would be less disruptive but less uniform.

findings.title: Several Procedure references accept new R6 target types not accepted by R4

oldState.summary: R4 reference targets were narrower for basedOn, report, and performer.actor.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 did not allow MedicationRequest as basedOn, Bundle as report, or CareTeam/HealthcareService as performer.actor.

newState.summary: R6 adds MedicationRequest to basedOn, Bundle to report, and CareTeam/HealthcareService to performer.actor.
newState.narrativeMd: These are additive target-domain changes, so R4 instances still validate upward, but R6 instances can use targets that R4 validators reject.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Additive reference target changes do not break existing R4 instances moving to R6. They can break R4-oriented code at runtime if it enumerates target resource types or rejects unknown target types, and they cannot be represented in base R4 without extension or alternative linkage.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Request/report/performer links affect workflow provenance and accountability.

justification.inferredGoal: Support additional workflow request, report packaging, and team/service performer patterns.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because the affected reference target lists are widened.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding MedicationRequest, Bundle, CareTeam, and HealthcareService targets is a plausible R6 expressiveness improvement. Since the R4 target types remain permitted, this finding is a downgrade and mixed-version interoperability concern rather than an R4-to-R6 breaking base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No R4-preserving alternative is needed for forward compatibility. Keeping the R4 target lists would improve R6-to-R4 round-tripping, but that would block the R6 target-domain goal rather than avoid invalidating old R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: All R4 targets remain allowed; the tradeoff is only that some R6 references cannot be represented in R4.

evidence.detail: R6 adds MedicationRequest to basedOn targets.
R6 adds Bundle to report targets.
R6 adds CareTeam and HealthcareService to performer.actor targets.

examples.examplesMd: Each shown target is accepted by the R6 Procedure StructureDefinition and outside the corresponding R4 target set.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 widens several reference domains. This is not a hard upward migration break but is a practical interoperability issue for mixed R4/R6 ecosystems and generated code with target-type enums.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: no. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: yes for the added targets. Strict R4 validators reject these references at the element target-profile level.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update target-type switches and database foreign-key assumptions. For R6→R4, either reject added targets, map to extensions, or represent the relationship through a different R4 resource where clinically appropriate.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The additive target changes are a reasonable non-breaking way to expand R6, but they still need explicit cross-version mapping rules.

findings.title: R6 adds bodyStructure, performer.period, recorded, reported[x], and supportingInfo with R4 round-trip impact

oldState.summary: R4 has no base elements corresponding to these R6 additions.
oldState.narrativeMd: Comparable R4 information may exist only in extensions, Provenance, related resources, or narrative.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional elements for target BodyStructure, performer timing, first recorded date, reported status/source, and generic supporting resources.

constraints.human: bodyStructure SHALL only be present if Procedure.bodySite is not present

newState.narrativeMd: `bodyStructure` is mutually exclusive with `bodySite`; `reported[x]` and `recorded` are summary elements; `supportingInfo` can reference any Resource.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not invalidate R4 instances in R6. They do create down-conversion loss because R4 has no base elements for performer-specific period, reported/source status, generic supportingInfo, or BodyStructure target. The new `con-4` invariant is a local R6 constraint, but it does not make old R4 instances invalid because `bodyStructure` did not exist in R4.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Reported/source status and supporting information can affect trust and interpretation; body-structure specificity can affect clinical localization.

justification.inferredGoal: Add commonly needed provenance, context, performer timing, and structured body-location capabilities.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because the listed elements are optional R6 additions.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional elements for body structure, performer period, recorded time, reported status/source, and supporting information improves native R6 expressiveness without making ordinary R4 Procedure instances invalid. The `bodyStructure` constraint only matters when new R6 content uses both body-location forms.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because these elements are optional additions, there is no R4-to-R6 break to avoid. Keeping them extension-only would make R6-to-R4 round-trip handling easier, but it would reduce discoverability and consistent validation of the new R6 content in the base resource.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extensions or backport mappings help downgrade, but they are migration mitigations rather than base R6 alternatives.

evidence.detail: R6 adds bodyStructure Reference(BodyStructure).
R6 adds performer.period Period.
R6 adds recorded dateTime.
R6 adds reported[x] boolean or Reference(Patient, RelatedPerson, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization).
R6 adds supportingInfo Reference(Resource).
R6 adds con-4 requiring bodyStructure only when bodySite is absent.

examples.examplesMd: R4 can preserve these facts only through extensions, related resources, or narrative; base elements do not exist.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds several optional Procedure elements. These are not breaking in the R4-to-R6 direction, but they are material for round-trip, serializers, and consumers that need to preserve all clinical/provenance content.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: no. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: yes when any added element is populated. `con-4` can reject R6 instances that populate both `bodySite` and `bodyStructure`, but that is not an inherited or R4-local break.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6→R4, define extensions or related-resource mappings for each populated added element. For R4→R6, consider whether existing extensions such as target-body-structure should be promoted to `bodyStructure`, while respecting con-4.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because the additions are optional, the R6 design is mostly backward compatible for upward migration. The unavoidable issue is down-conversion loss.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review existing R4 extensions, especially body-structure-related extensions, before choosing an automated mapping.

findings.title: Example bindings changed for performer.function and used; required status codes appear unchanged

oldState.summary: R4 performer.function used example ValueSet performer-role; usedCode used example ValueSet device-kind; status had required event-status|4.0.1.
oldState.narrativeMd: Only Procedure.status is a required binding among these changed local bindings.

newState.summary: R6 performer.function uses example ValueSet participant-role; used uses example ValueSet device-type; status has required event-status|6.0.0-ballot4 with the same code list in local CodeSystem files.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local CodeSystem-event-status concept codes were compared directly and matched. SNOMED-filtered example ValueSets were not expanded.

newState.narrativeMd: The example binding changes can affect picklists and generated terminology helpers, but not base validation unless a profile strengthens them.

facts.note: example strength and element changed to CodeableReference
required strength; local CodeSystem code list unchanged

impact.impactRationaleMd: The changed performer/function and used bindings are example strength, so base validators do not reject codes solely because of these ValueSet changes. The required `status` binding changed version labels, but the local ValueSet compose includes the same event-status CodeSystem and the local CodeSystem concepts match code-for-code. Risk remains for generated enums/picklists, profile-derived validators, and terminology servers using expanded value sets.

justification.inferredGoal: Refresh example terminology to broader/current value sets and align status with R6 package version.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because the changed local bindings are example-strength or preserve the required status code set.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Refreshing example ValueSets for performer function and used-item coding is normal terminology maintenance, and the required Procedure status codes appear unchanged in the local packages. These changes may affect generated UI lists or profile-derived bindings, but they do not identify a base R4-to-R6 instance break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because example bindings do not constrain base validation and the required status code list is preserved, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable. Systems that need old picklists can pin local or profile-level value sets, but that is implementation configuration rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Local picklist stability remains an implementation/profile concern, not a base validation compatibility issue.

evidence.detail: R4 performer.function example binding is performer-role.
R6 performer.function example binding is participant-role.
R4 status required binding is event-status|4.0.1.
R6 status required binding is event-status|6.0.0-ballot4.
Local R4 and R6 event-status CodeSystems contain the same eight codes: preparation, in-progress, not-done, on-hold, stopped, completed, entered-in-error, unknown.
evidence.quote: preparation | in-progress | not-done | on-hold | stopped | completed | entered-in-error | unknown

examples.examplesMd: No old-valid/new-invalid base-instance example was identified for status because the required code set appears unchanged. Example binding changes may still alter UI choices.

findings.narrativeMd: Terminology changed, but the main base-validation concern—Procedure.status—does not appear to remove or add required codes in the local package. The other changed bindings are example strength and should be treated as implementation guidance rather than hard validation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: no base validation break found for status codes. Runtime/codegen risk: low to medium for systems that generated enums or UI picklists from example ValueSets or assumed the exact binding canonical.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not change status-code migration rules based only on the versioned ValueSet URL. Refresh terminology helpers and picklists for performer.function and used, and separately evaluate any profiles that strengthened these example bindings.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The status binding version update is necessary for R6 packaging. Example binding updates are backward-compatible at the base validation layer.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: SNOMED-based example ValueSets were not expanded; a terminology server comparison could identify picklist differences.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 StructureDefinition is present at the assigned path with the same canonical URL, id, type, kind, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract=false flag as R4.
No local minimum cardinality increases were found for existing Procedure elements. Material maximum/cardinality changes are reported for `outcome` and `category`.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value changes were found on Procedure elements.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex-like value-limit changes were found on Procedure elements.
No local slicing definitions or slicing changes were found for Procedure elements.

Existing local modifier flags such as `status` remained materially stable. The new R6 `Procedure.focus` is modifier=true and is covered in a finding because it changes consumer obligations when present.

The required `Procedure.status` binding points to the R6 version of event-status, but local CodeSystem codes matched the R4 set. Example binding changes were identified but are not base validation breaks without profiles.
Local new constraints `prc-1` and `con-4` were found and reported where material. Inherited DomainResource/Element/Extension constraint expression differences were excluded as base-artifact changes.
